rationale: This is a cosmetic variant of the archive's strongest signal (Operating-Income Cash Cushion Yield), since a 3-year minimum of a slow-moving cash/(at+dlc) ratio will rank almost identically to its current level, so little new information is added.

Internally consistent and mechanically clean, but it is just the archive's Operating-Income Cash Cushion Yield with its numerator replaced by the already-tested Core-Consistency Operating Yield (fmb 2.4, alpha ≈ 0), so the most likely outcome is a mild dilution of a known result rather than new evidence.

It reuses the exact template of the archive's Low-Depreciation Cash Operating Yield — MUL(operating yield, SUMRANK(cash cushion, X)) — merely swapping X from -dp/at to -Δdebt/at, and the debt-change term was already shown to add little in Deleveraging Residual Claim Yield.

This is the archive's Profit-Funded Equity Payout Yield with the same ubiquitous cash-cushion term appended via SUMRANK, an incremental add-on rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the ib−Δceq construct is itself a well-known net-payout-yield proxy.

The gross-profit coverage of SG&A plus interest is a genuinely new conditioning term (distinct from prior SG&A-intensity and interest-trend variants) and the sign logic is coherent, though it is partly mechanically redundant with the operating margin already embedded in the operating-income yield leg.

Sign direction and expression are internally consistent, and the sale-plus-cash denominator combined with an explicit cash-drawdown term is a materially different construction from the prior glamour-fade signals, though it sits in a family where past fmb and alpha evidence has repeatedly disagreed.
